lessons: Start with provocative statements rather than descriptive setup; hooks that present a surprising paradox or vivid danger (like tuna meat vs. cod or pineapple eating you back) yield high start performance.
Eliminate immediate exposition in the first 10% of the script; lines that explain mechanics or background too early (seen in maple syrup and potato videos) trigger massive viewer drops exceeding 30%.
Avoid redundant phrasing and repetitive statements in early transition lines; repeating information causes immediate viewer fatigue and drop-off.

Ensure mid-video pacing remains tight; pauses, prompts to guess, or slow narrative detours around the 50% mark lead to steep audience loss (e.g., the sharp drop in the maple syrup and finger pruning videos).
worst_moment_types: Slow mechanical explanations and background definitions delivered right after the hook
Repetitive restatements of the same concept in consecutive lines
Mid-video pauses and direct prompts for the viewer to guess
best_hook_types: Striking biological contrasts comparing two familiar items (e.g., tuna vs. cod)
Urgent, visceral framing of a common experience as a defensive threat (e.g., pineapples eating you back)
